column3: Monthly verification that newer SDKs publish .NET 10, 9, and 8 applications with the expected patched runtimes; required older-runtime feeds must already be configured.

column4: Trigger
Resolve the current user's portable home directory.
Locate Visual Studio devenv.exe.
Discover the active .NET SDK version at runtime (must be a .NET 10.x SDK), instead of hardcoding a specific patch.
Launch a dedicated command prompt in the home directory.
Bring the command prompt to the foreground.
Clean the workspace then run dotnet --info and signal completion only when the required SDK version is present.
column6: ["(if exist MyGlobal rmdir /s /q MyGlobal) & dotnet --info > dotnet-info.txt && findstr /c:\"{vars.sdk}\" dotnet-info.txt >nul && title DOTNET_INFO_DONE"]

column4: Execute dotnet --info.
Wait for dotnet --info to confirm the required SDK.
Create the MyGlobal solution and signal completion.
Execute the solution creation command.
Wait for solution creation to complete.
Enter MyGlobal and create global.json.
column6: ["cd MyGlobal && dotnet new globaljson && title GLOBAL_JSON_CREATED"]

column4: Execute the global.json creation command.
Wait for global.json creation to complete.
Set global.json to the discovered SDK version and signal completion.
Execute the global.json update command.
Wait for global.json to be updated.
Verify global.json contains the pinned SDK version.
Create the test directory and publish the .NET 10 console application for win-x86.
column6: ["mkdir test && cd test && dotnet new console -o net10 -f net10.0 && cd net10 && dotnet publish -r win-x86 --self-contained && title NET10_PUBLISH_DONE"]

column4: Execute the .NET 10 create and publish command.
Wait for the .NET 10 publish to complete.
Open net10.deps.json in Visual Studio.
Capture net10.deps.json open in Visual Studio.
Verify net10.deps.json uses a .NET 10 runtime pack.
Close Visual Studio.
Return to the test directory then create and publish the .NET 9 console application for win-x86.
column6: ["cd .. && dotnet new console -o net9 -f net9.0 && cd net9 && dotnet publish -r win-x86 --self-contained && title NET9_PUBLISH_DONE"]

column4: Execute the .NET 9 create and publish command.
Wait for the .NET 9 publish to complete.
Open net9.deps.json in Visual Studio.
Capture net9.deps.json open in Visual Studio.
Verify net9.deps.json uses a .NET 9 runtime pack.
Close Visual Studio.
Return to the test directory then create and publish the .NET 8 console application for win-x86.
column6: ["cd .. && dotnet new console -o net8 -f net8.0 && cd net8 && dotnet publish -r win-x86 --self-contained && title NET8_PUBLISH_DONE"]

column4: Execute the .NET 8 create and publish command.
Wait for the .NET 8 publish to complete.
Open net8.deps.json in Visual Studio.
Capture net8.deps.json open in Visual Studio.
Verify net8.deps.json uses a .NET 8 runtime pack.
Close the test's Visual Studio and command-prompt windows.
